title: CloudFormation: Infrastructure as Code
description: Learn to define and provision AWS infrastructure using CloudFormation templates with resources, parameters, outputs, and intrinsic functions.

data.text: AWS CloudFormation is a service that lets you define your cloud infrastructure in code. You write a template file (JSON or YAML) that describes all the AWS resources you need, and CloudFormation provisions and configures them for you automatically.

A CloudFormation template is a JSON or YAML file that describes your resources. A stack is a collection of resources managed as a single unit. When you update a stack, CloudFormation creates a change set so you can preview changes before applying them.

Parameters let you pass values to your template at runtime, making templates reusable across environments. Outputs export values from your stack, such as resource IDs or URLs, that can be used by other stacks or displayed in the console.

data.title: Common Intrinsic Functions
items: **Fn::Ref** — references parameters or resource logical IDs
**Fn::GetAtt** — retrieves attributes from resources (e.g., S3 bucket ARN)
**Fn::Sub** — substitutes variables in strings, similar to template literals
**Fn::Join** — concatenates a list of values with a delimiter
**Fn::If** — conditionally returns one of two values

data.text: Nested stacks let you break large templates into smaller, reusable components. StackSets let you deploy the same CloudFormation stack across multiple AWS accounts and Regions, useful for enterprise-wide deployments.

data.title: CloudFormation Drift Detection
data.text: CloudFormation can detect drift — changes made to resources outside of CloudFormation. This helps identify configuration changes that may have been made manually and could cause stack inconsistencies.

terms.definition: A JSON or YAML file that describes the AWS resources you want to create.
A collection of AWS resources created and managed as a single unit from a CloudFormation template.
A summary of proposed changes to a stack that lets you preview the impact before executing.
A special CloudFormation function (e.g., Ref, GetAtt, Sub) that performs operations on template values.

data.description: Write a CloudFormation template that provisions an S3 bucket, an IAM user, and a DynamoDB table.

Include an S3::Bucket resource with versioning enabled
Include a DynamoDB::Table with a partition key
Deploy the stack using the CloudFormation console or AWS CLI
data.expectedOutcome: The stack is created with all three resources. You can view them in the AWS console and verify outputs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CloudFormation defines infrastructure as code in JSON or YAML
Stacks are the unit of deployment and management
Parameters make templates reusable across environments
Nested stacks and StackSets help organize and replicate infrastructure
data.takeaway: CloudFormation is the foundation of reproducible AWS infrastructure. Once your infrastructure is code, you can version it, review it, and deploy it reliably.
